chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribat said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever has a debt and intends to pay it off, two angels will be with him from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic and Exalted, assisting him in fulfilling his obligation. If he falls short in his intention to pay, they will fall short in assisting him by the measure of what was lacking from his intention.'
ai.seo_question: How does intention affect divine assistance in repaying debt according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib al-ahkam*, this narration by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the metaphysical reality of divine guardianship (*hufaz*) for those with sincere financial intent, linking spiritual state to material ease. It underscores the Shia principle that *niyyah* (intention) is not merely internal but actively influences external circumstances, offering comfort to debtors who may face temporary hardship despite their resolve.
